frozen_original.title: Trump Pursues Retaliatory Investigation of Former CIA Director Gina Haspel
frozen_original.synopsis: In 2025, the Trump administration launched an investigation into former CIA Director Gina Haspel, alleging she was responsible for classified leaks damaging to Trump, in what critics described as a retaliatory prosecution targeting a career intelligence official who had refused to assist Trump's political objectives during his first term. Haspel had previously refused Trump's requests to classify and suppress intelligence assessments and had been involved in decisions about the Ukraine whistleblower complaint. Legal observers noted that targeting former intelligence officials for authorized disclosures or for declining to participate in illegal activities represented a profound chilling effect on the entire intelligence community. Former CIA officials described the investigation as an attempt to criminalize professional independence.

This remains an internal, unverified allegation.
primary.description_long: The frozen record alleges that the Trump administration opened a classified-leak investigation of former CIA Director Gina Haspel on March 20, 2025, over leaks said to have damaged President Trump. It frames the alleged inquiry as retaliation and says critics linked it to Haspel’s earlier handling of intelligence assessments and the Ukraine whistleblower matter. None of those asserted connections is established by the supplied packet: it identifies no agency announcement, case number, charge, named source, or contemporaneous report confirming that a leak investigation was opened. A July 28, 2025 Federalist article reports that Peter Schweizer raised questions about Haspel and argues in its headline that she should be investigated over Russia-related matters. That later commentary does not document a March leak inquiry, and its topic is distinct from the record’s alleged classified-leak probe. This draft preserves the supplied claim as an allegation for internal review. Its date and all attributed conduct remain unverified; do not present them as findings, charges, or proof of retaliation. frozen_original.title: Trump Cuts CDC Budget by 40% — Ends Disease Surveillance Programs
frozen_original.synopsis: In March 2025, the Trump administration proposed and began implementing a 40 percent reduction in the CDC's annual budget, eliminating or gutting programs including the Epidemiology and Laboratory Capacity program used for outbreak detection, the National Center for Chronic Disease Prevention, global disease surveillance programs in 49 countries, and the Public Health Emergency Preparedness cooperative agreements with states. CDC staff were placed on administrative leave and then fired en masse as part of DOGE-directed cuts. The gutted surveillance infrastructure meant the U.S. would have reduced capacity to detect novel pathogens, track disease outbreaks, or coordinate pandemic responses. Former CDC directors from both Republican and Democratic administrations co-signed a letter warning the cuts posed an existential threat to American public health readiness.

primary.title: April 2025 Trump Administration Plan Proposed Cutting the CDC Budget by More Than 40%
primary.description_short: CNN reported an April 10 internal plan proposed a CDC budget reduction of more than 40%; the draft could change and was not an enacted cut.
primary.description_medium: An internal federal health-agency document dated April 10, 2025, proposed reducing the CDC budget by more than 40%, CNN reported on April 16. CNN said the draft could still be finalized with changes and would consolidate health programs into a proposed Administration for a Healthy America. This corrected card concerns a proposal, not a March cut already in effect or proof that every surveillance program named in the original synopsis ended.
primary.description_long: CNN reported on April 16, 2025, that an internal Trump administration document dated April 10 outlined a proposed reduction of more than 40% in the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s budget. The document also previewed a broader restructuring of federal health agencies and consolidation of programs into a proposed Administration for a Healthy America. CNN reported that the plan could still be finalized with changes and described the reductions as what would happen “if enacted as is.” The evidence supports a proposed budget action; it does not show that the CDC had already received a 40% reduction in March. Nor does the accessed reporting substantiate that every program named in the original synopsis—including outbreak-detection grants, chronic-disease programs, global surveillance across 49 countries, and state emergency-preparedness agreements—was eliminated by this same proposal. This card therefore focuses on the April 10 proposal and leaves implementation unresolved. It does not combine the proposal, agency layoffs, and program closures into one completed event. The percentage is CNN’s description of the administration’s plan, not a final appropriation or an independently audited spending change.

corrected_proposal.title: April 2025 Trump Administration Plan Proposed Cutting the CDC Budget by More Than 40%
corrected_proposal.description_short: CNN reported an April 10 internal plan proposed a CDC budget reduction of more than 40%; the draft could change and was not an enacted cut.
corrected_proposal.description_medium: An internal federal health-agency document dated April 10, 2025, proposed reducing the CDC budget by more than 40%, CNN reported on April 16. CNN said the draft could still be finalized with changes and would consolidate health programs into a proposed Administration for a Healthy America. This corrected card concerns a proposal, not a March cut already in effect or proof that every surveillance program named in the original synopsis ended.
corrected_proposal.description_long: CNN reported on April 16, 2025, that an internal Trump administration document dated April 10 outlined a proposed reduction of more than 40% in the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s budget. The document also previewed a broader restructuring of federal health agencies and consolidation of programs into a proposed Administration for a Healthy America. CNN reported that the plan could still be finalized with changes and described the reductions as what would happen “if enacted as is.” The evidence supports a proposed budget action; it does not show that the CDC had already received a 40% reduction in March. Nor does the accessed reporting substantiate that every program named in the original synopsis—including outbreak-detection grants, chronic-disease programs, global surveillance across 49 countries, and state emergency-preparedness agreements—was eliminated by this same proposal. This card therefore focuses on the April 10 proposal and leaves implementation unresolved. It does not combine the proposal, agency layoffs, and program closures into one completed event. The percentage is CNN’s description of the administration’s plan, not a final appropriation or an independently audited spending change.

frozen_original.title: Trump administration reinstates family separation policy separating immigrant children from parents
frozen_original.synopsis: The Trump administration reinstated its family separation policy, again deliberately separating parents from children at the border as a punitive deterrence measure despite widespread condemnation. The policy separated thousands of families, with children placed in government facilities while parents faced criminal prosecution for illegal entry. The administration acknowledged the separations were intentional policy and explicitly rejected concerns about the psychological harm to children. Pediatricians and child welfare experts warned the policy constituted government-inflicted child abuse.

blockers.detail: The frozen claim says that on April 1, 2025 the administration formally reinstated the 2018 zero-tolerance family-separation policy and separated thousands of families while prosecuting parents. The supplied AP URL is about Alien Enemies Act deportation flights, not family separation. The accessible April Guardian report documents renewed family detention, including families held at Karnes and Dilley, but does not establish that the government separated those parents and children from one another or formally reinstated zero tolerance. The later August 2025 reporting found in search concerns a different, later tactic and cannot repair the April date. No same-event narrower claim or quantity is supportable from this packet.
